newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels say won't be pressured to compromise.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say won't be pressured to compromise.

text.p: Zaire's rebels on Monday denounced Western pressure on them to compromise with the regime of President Mobutu Sese Seko and what they said was the arrival of 400 Chinese troops in Kinshasa to bolster the dictatorship.

The rebels' choice for finance minister, Mwana Nanga Mawanpanga, reading a statement from rebel leader Laurent Kabila, said the alliance had "learned of the arrival of large contingents of Chinese troops in Kinshasa. We know of 400 troops at present."
He said Kabila would resist all pressure to compromise with Mobutu and rebel fighters would now regard any foreign soldiers on Zairean soil as a target.

He declined to say which Western powers were pressing Kabila to compromise with Mobutu, but he stressed that the alliance would not stop its offensive to take the capital Kinshasa until Mobutuu signed his resignation.
